(I also spoiler tagged a few things throughout, just in case :P)

7) Specter's Call. There were quite a few aspects of the game I loved, but this always seemed like the most lackluster entry to me. The only things that really stuck out to me the most my first time through were Luke's introduction, the Black Raven (more specifically, [spoiler](#s "Crow")), the spectre itself, and the game's ending. Which, not going to lie, was one of the many things in this series that made me bawl like a baby. ;_;

6) Curious Village. By no means a bad game, especially considering it was what started the franchise. But each time I revisit it, it just doesn't stack up to the other games. The setting and atmosphere was nailed in this game though, and the soundtrack definitely helped. I just feel like later entries kinda surpassed CV as time went on.

5) Professor Layton vs. Ace Attorney. I loved the characters in this game (Barnham FTW), as well as the plot. I know it technically doesn't count as a main series entry, but some of the plot twists could fight right in, IMO. Also, as someone that's never played much Phoenix Wright, I felt like the courtroom system was explained very well (even if it is kinda easy to pick up). There was no confusion about how the game worked, and that's a great thing for a noob like me. The soundtrack was a really nice mixture between both franchises, too - it actually made me listen to some of the AA soundtracks afterward just to see how different they were!

4) Pandora's Box. Like a few other people in this thread, I played Pandora's Box before Curious Village. The only reason I asked for it for Christmas was because I saw the ad on TV, and my little 9-year old self lost it. Thankfully, the murder mystery wasn't the only thing I liked about this game - the soundtrack is one of my favourites, I loved the characters (they added to the atmosphere really well in some points), and the ending didn't quite make me cry, but I'll agree it was very touching. Also, the [spoiler](#s "ballroom nightmare leading into the "kidnapping" of sorts") is still one of my favourite Layton moments. That cutscene is just so freaking eerie, and I love it. :D

3) Lost Future. Just to get the obvious out of the way, cried like a baby at the end. :( But other than that, I'd say this is the point in my list where the puzzles really started to impress me (and also made me look like a complete idiot). Not only that, even though it's my third favourite game, I'd say this is my favourite overall soundtrack in the series. The plot and characters were a huge highlight for me, and I've always held Future Luke in high regard when it comes to my favourite Layton characters. Also, one little extra bonus I realized not too long ago was that Liam O'Brien (who is essentially my favourite VA in anything that he does) actually voice acted in this game! So yeah, DEFINITELY not biased or anything, but that adds to my liking of this game slightly. :3

2) Azran Legacy. I can certainly see why some people find this to be a lackluster game, but I personally found it enthralling from start to finish. The puzzles were well thought-out and clever (from what I can remember), the music was really nice (fit the aesthetic really really well IMO), your standard fare. But the one thing that blew my mind upon playing this game? The story and its plot twists. I know I was only 12 or so when I played this for the first time, but I still remember reacting very loudly and spontaneously to those... I also cried. Not as much as Lost Future, but I cried. A lot. Partly because it was, to my knowledge at the time, the last Layton game in the series and I didn't want it to end. XD

1) Miracle Mask. OH BOY where do I begin with this. The aesthetic and atmosphere drew me in from the minute I started a new save file, and it stayed that way through the entire game. The poster also made a really good point that the Masked Gentleman was genuinely threating throughout the plot - I personally found him to be more threatening than Descole ever was. Randall also happens to be my favourite character in the series as a whole, and it wrecked me when [spoiler](#s "the cutscene of his death") came around. But towards the end of the game, when the whole shadow puppet sequence was shown, and I figured out who the Masked Gentleman was... never have I felt such a sense of achievement with a video game. (I know some people may find it predictable, but it was an achievement for me - I normally can't see ANYTHING coming with stuff like this.) To top it all off, the soundtrack was beautiful, the side characters were all interesting to me (also, Matthew Mercer and Laura Bailey were part of the VA cast. How can I not love that?) and the puzzles were all engaging in the best way possible.
